Chapter 4: How Joy in God Changes Prayer, Marriage, and Everyday Life.
Picture this—it's the end of a long, exhausting day. You’re alone for a moment, just sitting there, thinking about all the challenges and disappointments that've stacked up. It’s so easy to turn inward, right? Maybe to worry, or just to distract yourself with something mindless. But imagine if, instead, a simple prayer rises in your heart. Not a prayer for things, or even for answers, but a quiet longing for a deeper sense of God’s presence.
That's when prayer starts to shift. It’s no longer just a list of requests. It becomes a way of reaching for joy in God Himself. Instead of trying to get God to do what we want, we’re actually seeking to find our satisfaction in Him. Sure, we still bring our needs and requests—but suddenly, they’re not the main thing. Deep down, what we really need isn’t more stuff or even more solutions. What our hearts are craving is God Himself.
And here’s where it gets interesting—this shift doesn’t just change how we pray. It touches every single part of life, especially our relationships. Take marriage, for example. It’s so common to look to your spouse for fulfillment. But when those expectations aren’t met, disappointment and frustration sneak in. What if, instead, both partners focused on finding their deepest joy in God? The whole dynamic changes. Love isn’t just about getting your needs met—it’s about sharing the joy that comes from God.
Let me tell you about a couple who tried this. After years of struggling, they made a decision: stop trying to change each other, and start looking for joy in God—together. The change didn’t happen overnight, but it was real. Arguments faded. Forgiveness came more easily. Their marriage stopped feeling like a battleground, and started feeling like a partnership—one where they were both chasing after joy.
But it doesn’t stop there. This perspective can transform the way you approach work, parenting, and all the ordinary routines. Suddenly, these aren’t just tasks to get through. They’re moments where you can actually experience and share God’s joy. Think of a parent, worn out from the chaos of raising kids—not just pushing through on willpower, but leaning into the quiet assurance that God’s joy is available, even in the mess.
Most of us don’t even realize how easily we slip into routines of duty and obligation. Life gets busy, and faith can feel like just another thing to check off the list. But when joy in God is at the center, even ordinary moments get a new kind of meaning. Work turns into worship. Relationships become spaces for grace. And challenges? They become invitations to trust.
There’s another shift, too. When suffering comes, it’s easy to wonder if God’s even there. But when you’re seeking joy in Him, pain isn’t the end of the story. It actually becomes a chance to go deeper. This doesn’t mean pretending everything’s fine, or denying the reality of hardship. It means finding hope right in the middle of it all. The promise isn’t that life will always be easy—it’s that God’s joy is there for you, even in the hardest moments.
